topicTitle: Assumptions, Inferences, and Courses of Action

questions.question:
Statement: Please keep your mobile phones switched off during the film.

Assumptions:
I. Mobile phones may disturb other viewers.
II. Everyone watching the film owns a mobile phone.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The request makes sense only if phones can disturb others (I implicit). It does not need everyone to own one (II is not needed). Answer: Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Buy one litre of milk from the store near the station.

Assumptions:
I. No other shop sells milk.
II. The store sells milk.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The instruction is pointless unless the store sells milk (II implicit). Other shops may sell milk too (I is not needed). Answer: Only II follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The manager asked all employees to submit their reports by Friday.

Assumptions:
I. The employees can complete the reports by Friday.
II. All employees dislike writing reports.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: A deadline presumes it can be met (I implicit). Dislike of reports is not needed (II). Answer: Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Use soap to wash your hands before meals.

Assumptions:
I. Everyone has dirty hands before meals.
II. Soap helps to remove germs from the hands.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The advice rests on soap removing germs (II implicit). It does not claim that everyone's hands are dirty (I is not needed). Answer: Only II follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The company advertised the job in newspapers.

Assumptions:
I. People read newspapers and may see the advertisement.
II. Only newspaper readers will be able to apply.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: Advertising in a newspaper assumes that people read it (I implicit). Others may hear of the job in other ways (II is not needed). Answer: Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Drive slowly in the school zone.

Assumptions:
I. Children never cross the road in the school zone.
II. Driving slowly reduces the chance of accidents.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The instruction assumes slow driving reduces accidents (II implicit). Children may well cross, which is why the instruction exists (I is false). Answer: Only II follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Avoid travelling by road at night in the hills; take the morning bus.

Assumptions:
I. Roads in the hills are risky at night.
II. Morning buses are available.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The advice rests on night travel being risky (I) and on morning buses existing (II). Both are implicit. Answer: Both I and II follow.

questions.question:
Statement: The government should introduce free school meals to improve attendance.

Assumptions:
I. Free meals will attract children to school.
II. School attendance is currently low.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The proposal assumes that free meals attract children (I) and that attendance needs improving (II). Both are implicit. Answer: Both I and II follow.

questions.question:
Statement: Mr Rao has asked the bank to waive the late fee because he paid his dues within two days of the due date.

Assumptions:
I. The bank has the power to waive late fees.
II. Banks never charge late fees.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The request presumes the bank can waive the fee (I implicit). If banks never charged late fees there would be nothing to waive (II is false). Answer: Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Smartphones should be given to students to improve their learning.

Assumptions:
I. Students will use smartphones only for learning.
II. Smartphones can help students learn.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The proposal assumes smartphones can aid learning (II implicit). It does not assume exclusive use for learning (I is too strong). Answer: Only II follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The factory produced 500 units in January and 600 units in February.

Inferences:
I. Production increased from January to February.
II. Production will increase again in March.

Which inference can be drawn from the statement?
questions.explanation: 600 is greater than 500, so production increased (I). The statement gives no basis for a prediction about March (II). Answer: Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: All the candidates who scored above 80% were given scholarships. Rita was given a scholarship.

Inferences:
I. Rita scored above 80%.
II. Only candidates who scored above 80% were given scholarships.

Which inference can be drawn from the statement?
questions.explanation: The statement does not say that scholarships were given only for scores above 80%, so Rita may have qualified another way. Neither inference is forced. Answer: Neither I nor II follows.

questions.question:
Statement: A school has 600 students, and 40% of them are girls.

Inferences:
I. There are 240 girls in the school.
II. There are 400 boys in the school.

Which inference can be drawn from the statement?
questions.explanation: 40% of 600 = 240 girls, so there are 360 boys, not 400 (II is false). Answer: Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The museum is open from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on all days except Mondays.

Inferences:
I. A visitor arriving at 6 p.m. on a Tuesday cannot enter.
II. The museum is open from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Mondays.

Which inference can be drawn from the statement?
questions.explanation: At 6 p.m. the museum is closed on Tuesday (I). It is closed on Mondays (II is false). Answer: Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: A large number of students of a college were found suffering from dengue.

Courses of action:
I. The college should be closed for a few days and the premises cleaned.
II. The students should be told to stay at home and not worry.

Which course of action should follow?
questions.explanation: Closing and cleaning deals with the cause of the outbreak (I). Asking students to stay at home without worry does nothing about the cause (II is weak). Answer: Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Prices of vegetables have risen sharply due to heavy rain.

Courses of action:
I. The government should ban the sale of vegetables.
II. The government should release stocks or arrange imports to bring prices down.

Which course of action should follow?
questions.explanation: Increasing supply addresses the price rise (II). Banning sales would worsen the problem (I is extreme). Answer: Only II follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Buy a ticket in advance to avoid long queues at the museum.

Assumptions:
I. Advance tickets are available.
II. There are long queues at the museum without an advance ticket.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The advice presumes that advance tickets exist (I) and that queues are otherwise long (II). Both are implicit. Answer: Both I and II follow.

questions.question:
Statement: Between 2015 and 2020 the number of vehicles in a city doubled while the length of its roads increased by only 10%.

Inferences:
I. The number of vehicles per kilometre of road increased.
II. The number of vehicles per kilometre of road more than doubled.

Which inference can be drawn from the statement?
questions.explanation: Vehicles rose 2 times and roads 1.1 times, so the density rose by 2 ÷ 1.1 ≈ 1.82 times: it increased (I) but did not more than double (II). Answer: Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The water level in the city's main reservoir has fallen to a critically low level.

Courses of action:
I. The authorities should wait for the monsoon before taking any step.
II. The authorities should start rationing the water supply immediately.

Which course of action should follow?
questions.explanation: Rationing now conserves the remaining water (II). Waiting leaves the shortage unmanaged (I is weak). Answer: Only II follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The company has decided to give a bonus to employees who complete the project before the deadline.

Assumptions:
I. The bonus will motivate the employees.
II. All employees can complete the project before the deadline.

Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: The bonus is meant to motivate (I implicit). The offer does not assume every employee will complete the project early (II is not needed). Answer: Only I follows.
